archetype.name: Lottery Team (defense-broken)
archetype.definition: A team whose genuine frontcourt star and foul-drawing offense can't come close to covering the league's worst defense, leaving it in the bottom tier of the conference with a margin that matches its record.

report.headline: Zion is elite, the defense is the league's worst, and November exposed it
report.take:
New Orleans is 4-10, 25th on the site, and the record is not a fluke in either direction. The W vs Pt Diff is exactly 0 and the margin implies four wins, the number it has. A Net Rtg of -8.8 ranks 25th. It belongs in the same company as the 2024-25 team that went 21-61 at -9.5, not the 2023-24 group that won 49 games at +4.5. The offense is only mildly below average, 20th with a 112.4 ORtg. The defense is the real problem: last in the league at 121.2, seven points worse than the league mean.

The season's shape is a split between two months. In October the Pelicans outscored opponents, 119.67 to 117.83 a game. They closed it on a four-game win streak, two of those wins in overtime. Then the floor gave way. November is 2-6 with 130.25 allowed a game. The last five are all losses by 28 a game, including 87-138 at Golden State and 111-145 against Brooklyn, part of a six-game losing streak that is still running. The injury list lines up with that slide. Trey Murphy III (+8 On-Off, 61.3 TS %) has played only 9 of 14 games and is Out. So are Dejounte Murray, Trendon Watford and Bryce McGowens. The sheet doesn't say exactly when each went down, but losing the second-best wing and a starting guard at once is how a thin roster turns into this.

What the numbers hide is how good the frontcourt is. Zion Williamson ranks 4th of 88 on the PF tab with a 67.6 TS %, a 3.1 BPM, a team-best 1.5 Win Shares and a +14.4 On-Off. That is why the frontcourt grades B+ while the backcourt (D+) and wings (D) sag. The offense lives at the line, with a league-best 37.2 FT Rate and the fewest threes of any team (33.3 3PA Rate, 30th). That style keeps its TS % slightly above league average despite a 32.8 3P %. The odd number is Herbert Jones: a 43.9 TS % and a -8.6 BPM, yet a +19.7 On-Off. He is almost certainly why opposing small forwards score less against New Orleans than against nearly anyone (15.71 a game, 2nd fewest).

On defense, everything else leaks. Opponents shoot 71.4% at the rim (29th, 6.3 points above the league). Opposing power forwards average 29.5 points (30th) and opposing point guards 30.86 (27th). The team also loses the glass at both ends. This is a third straight bad defense, after 29th in 2024-25 and 25th in 2025-26, so it is a structural problem rather than a sample-size blip. It won't fix itself with health alone.

strengths.title: Zion anchors a B+ frontcourt
strengths.body: Williamson is producing at an elite clip: 4th of 88 on the PF tab, 67.6 TS % on 23.5 USG %, and the team is far better with him on the floor. Karlo Matković adds hyper-efficient finishing (69.2 TS %) behind him. As long as Zion stays on the court this is the one group that wins its minutes. Thirteen of 14 games played is a healthy start.

strengths.title: Free throws prop up efficiency
strengths.body: A league-best FT Rate of 37.2, 8.7 above the league, is the offense's identity. It is a rim-attack, bully-ball attack built around Zion and Derik Queen. That style is sustainable because it comes from shot profile, not shooting luck. It is also why TS % ranks 13th even with a 25th-ranked 3P %. The ceiling is capped by the fewest threes in the league.

strengths.title: Herb Jones locks down wings
strengths.body: Opposing small forwards get only 15.71 points a game against New Orleans, 2nd fewest in the league. Jones's +19.7 On-Off says his defense swings games even though his box-score line (43.9 TS %, -8.6 BPM) is ugly. That kind of on-court impact usually holds up better than shooting slumps do.

concerns.title: Worst defense in the league
concerns.body: A 121.2 DRtg ranks 30th, driven by rim defense: opponents shoot 71.4% within four feet (29th) and get there often (31.3 Opp Rim Rate, 22nd). Opposing power forwards average 29.5 points, the most in the league. History says this is real. The defense was 29th and 25th the last two seasons, and this year's rim number is worse than any of the last five.

concerns.title: November collapse, injury list growing
concerns.body: Over the last five, opponents put up 136 points a game, 11.07 more than the season average, during a six-game losing streak. Murphy (+8 On-Off) and Murray are both Out, which forces more minutes onto the weakest groups. Some of the blowout scale will ease. But the October version of this team had healthier wings, and that version isn't coming back this week.

concerns.title: Backcourt creation is a liability
concerns.body: Jeremiah Fears carries a 25.2 USG % on a 51.7 TS % with a -3.8 BPM and a -8 On-Off. That is the profile of a young guard learning on the job, not one carrying an offense. With Murray out, the D+ backcourt has no efficient creator. It also has little spacing to give Zion: the 32.8 3P % ranks 25th.

trend.note: A competitive October with a positive margin and a four-game win streak has given way to a 2-6 November and five straight lopsided losses. The defense is giving up 136 a game in that stretch.

weekAhead.headline: Four winning teams, then a Phoenix game that matters
weekAhead.body:
This is a brutal five-game stretch for a team on a six-game skid. It opens with Golden State, who beat New Orleans by 51 last week, and Detroit at home. Then come back-to-back road nights at Oklahoma City and San Antonio. The Spurs are 12-2 with a 13.0 Net Rtg (2nd) and a top-three defense. The Thunder allow opponents just 56.7% at the rim, best in the league. Those two games hit the Pelicans' rim-and-free-throw offense exactly where it lives, and the second comes on no rest.

The realistic targets are Detroit, whose defense is soft against power forwards, and the closer, Phoenix. The Suns are 5-7 with a 26th-ranked defense, the league's worst DRB %, and they allow the most points to opposing point guards. That is a game New Orleans can win by crashing the glass and turning Fears loose. One or two wins would be a decent week. Another winless run is very possible if the rim defense doesn't stiffen.

keyMatchups.title: Zion against elite rim protection
keyMatchups.body: OKC (56.7%, 1st) and San Antonio (59.5%, 3rd) are the best teams in the league at finishing defense near the basket. San Antonio also gives up the fewest points to power forwards. If Zion's interior game gets walled off, the league's lowest-volume three-point team has no Plan B.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's soft spot at power forward
keyMatchups.body: The Pistons allow 25.17 points a game to power forwards (25th) and big rebounding nights there. That is Zion's lane in an otherwise stingy defense (110.3 DRtg, 6th). Detroit forces turnovers at the 4th-highest rate, so ball security for Fears matters.

keyMatchups.title: Phoenix's glass and guard defense
keyMatchups.body: The Suns have the league's worst DRB % (66.9) and RPG, and they allow 32.92 points a game to point guards, also 30th. A 26th-ranked ORB % team should still find second chances here. This is the week's best shot at snapping the streak.

weekAhead.watch: Opponent rim finishing. If New Orleans can't drag its 71.4% Opp Rim FG % toward the league's 65.1, the blowouts continue regardless of who returns.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace carries to 23 wins, and the underlying profile supports something close to that. The margin and the record agree, there's no close-game luck to unwind, and the defense has been bottom-six for three seasons running. Getting Murphy and Murray back should pull the team out of the 136-allowed territory of the last five games and closer to its October level. But even that version was a below-.500 team. A rest-of-season Net Rtg in the -9 to -5 range and roughly 20 to 27 wins is the realistic band.

The free-throw-heavy offense and Zion's efficiency are sustainable; the 32.8 3P % may tick up modestly. The upside case needs a healthy Zion, a healthy wing group, and Fears growing into his usage. The downside is another 21-61-style season if the injuries linger.

confidence.note: Only 14 games, but the defense matches two prior seasons of evidence.
